title: How do we find the areas of three triangles?
description: Three triangles are given with a base and a height, one of them a right triangle. Each area is half of base times height, and each is checked against a rectangle on the same base and height.
teaching_notes: One idea: the area of a triangle is half of base times height, where the height meets the base at a right angle. Watch for children who multiply a slanted side by a base.

video_script.why: The child uses half of base times height for three triangles, picking the height that meets the base at a right angle, and in a right triangle using the two shorter sides.
video_script.substitution: Take half of the base times the height for each triangle, and check with the rectangle on the same base and height.
video_script.anchor: the three triangles of the book, with bases and heights marked
video_script.payoff_line: the three areas are six, eight and six square centimetres

final_answer.spoken: six, eight and six square centimetres

hold_back: the three areas are 6 cm², 8 cm² and 6 cm²
never_show: the three areas together, before the answer beat
maths_rules: (i) base BC = 4 cm, height AE = 3 cm: 1/2 × 4 × 3 = 6 cm²
(ii) base EF = 5 cm, height DN = 3.2 cm drawn to EF: 1/2 × 5 × 3.2 = 1/2 × 16 = 8 cm²
(iii) right triangle NAT with NA = 4 cm and AT = 3 cm: the two legs are a base and its height: 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²
check: rectangles on the same base and height have areas 4 × 3 = 12, 5 × 3.2 = 16, 3 × 4 = 12; half of each is 6, 8, 6
video_script.design: One idea: area of a triangle is half of base times height. The three triangles stay on stage. Each is worked in turn and then checked with a rectangle on the same base and height.
open_questions: The book figures are not in the extracted text. The worklist gives base BC = 4 cm with height AE = 3 cm for part (i), base EF = 5 cm with height DN = 3.2 cm for part (ii), and legs NA = 4 cm and AT = 3 cm for part (iii); the pictures should be checked against these readings.
